newsitem.title: USA: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS--prices flat/firm, look to NYC.
newsitem.headline: U.S MUNICIPAL FOCUS--prices flat/firm, look to NYC.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds in late trade on Monday mainly were pegged from flat to about one one-eighth of a point higher in spots, as the market looked ahead to New York City's $900 million tax exempt bond sale.

But prices for the city's bonds failed to increase with the gains seen in a few other sectors of the municipal market, as traders, despite fairly strong retail interest, positioned themselves ahead of New York City's Wednesday sale, which includes about $122 million of taxable bonds.
"New York lagged a lot, just in anticipation of the deal," a trader said.

Still, because of its size and the liquidity that creates, traders said New York City was expected to outdraw other New York State authority issuers, including the nearly $186 million sale of revenue bonds by the Metropolitan Transportation Authority, a New York State body, which runs the city's subway system.
"We've had very good reception on city's," a trader said.

Further, there was speculation that the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey, which might delay a $920 million bond sale by a couple of weeks or so until late April, mainly would be offered to institutional investors.
"It's a special deal, it's managers only," a trader said.
A spokesman for the Port Authority referred calls to Lehman Brothers, which is underwriting the deal with Citibank, and brokerage house officials were not immediately available to comment.

With the week's offerings expected to surge to around $4.5 bilion, traders also were awaiting a few other key deals, including Georgia's $307 million sale on Tuesday, the biggest competitive deal planned for the week.
Further, Puerto Rico was expected to tap the market for $260.7 million of revenue bonds.

U.S. Treasury bond prices held most of their gains in late afternoon trade, bolstered by the strong dollar. The June Treasury bond contract rose 20 ticks to 107-20/32, while the June municipal bond futures lagged, only rising 12 ticks to 112-3/32. This left the MOB spread at plus 143 ticks.

In the secondary market, actively quoted issues included Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority Refunding Revolving Fund of April 2027, which pay a 6-1/8 percent coupon, and were bid at 98-3/4, up a quarter of a point.
And Texas State Turnpike Authority Dallas North Thruway Revenues of January 2023, which pay a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.88 percent, NET, down two basis points.
